# Gravity and energy {#sec-ch06}

Gravity does work on the flow, and a finite-volume code has to decide where to book it. This chapter is about
that decision and what each answer costs. It covers the cell form, which applies the body force and the work
$\rho v_1g_1$ in the same cell; the face form, which books the work as a flux difference of potential energy
across the cell's $x_1$ faces; the global fixer that repairs the cell form's budget once per step; the
corrected-PE face work, which makes the booked work fourth-order consistent with the scheme's own mass fluxes;
the gravity work inside the vertical implicit operator; and a closing comparison of what each form conserves and
which diagnostic measures it. The momentum equation is the same in every form; only the energy row changes. The
hydrostatic reference state these forms are often used with is @sec-ch05, and the implicit solver they couple into
is the vertical implicit solve of the time-integration chapter.

**One identity behind every form.** Every form in this chapter is one identity with a different choice of
discrete potential energy, so it is derived once, here, before the forms that use it.

**The continuous budget.** With constant gravity $g_1$ along $x_1$, mass and total energy obey the continuity
equation and the total-energy equation in their usual form,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\partial_t\rho + \nabla\cdot(\rho\mathbf v) &= 0, \\
\partial_tE + \nabla\cdot\big[(E+p)\mathbf v\big] &= \rho v_1g_1 ,
\end{aligned}
$$

with $E$ the total energy density [J m$^{-3}$]. The $x_2$, $x_3$ components of gravity book cell work only and play
no part here. The potential $\phi(x_1) = -g_1x_1$ [m$^2$ s$^{-2}$] does not depend on time, and
$\rho v_1g_1 = -\rho\mathbf v\cdot\nabla\phi$, so $E+\rho\phi$ is conserved:

$$
\partial_t(E+\rho\phi) + \nabla\cdot\big[(E+p+\rho\phi)\mathbf v\big] = 0 .
$$

In a closed domain $\int(E+\rho\phi)\,\mathrm{d}V$ is constant. Throughout the chapter, an invariant written
"$E+P$" or "$E+\mathrm{PE}_d$" means the integrated sum $\sum_iV_iE_i + P$ [J, per unit horizontal area on
Cartesian grids and per steradian on spherical-polar and cubed-sphere grids], with $P$ a discrete potential energy
of the same units.

**The exact work in one cell.** Integrate the gravity source over cell $i$ and write the $x_1$ mass flux density as
$F=\rho v_1$ [kg m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$]: $\int_{V_i}\rho v_1g_1\,\mathrm{d}V = g_1V_i\langle F\rangle_{V_i}$. Multiply the
continuity equation by $\phi$ and integrate over the cell, using
$\phi\,\nabla\cdot(\rho\mathbf v) = \nabla\cdot(\phi\rho\mathbf v) - \rho\mathbf v\cdot\nabla\phi$ and the divergence
theorem. Only the $x_1$ faces matter: on Cartesian, spherical-polar and gnomonic-equiangle grids the $x_2$, $x_3$
faces join cells of the same $x_1$ level (on the cubed sphere, the same radius:
`docs/derivations/curved-gravity-work-weight.md@6fbb39750f62b83df096058a4746e77d0a634bc5` §12.6), so their terms
are mass fluxes times one value of $\phi$, which @sec-ch06-dwork treats with the horizontal directions. Rearranged,
the exact gravity work in a cell is

$$
\begin{aligned}
g_1V_i\langle F\rangle_{V_i} &= -\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\mathcal P_i - \Delta_i[A\phi F], \\
\mathcal P_i &= \int_{V_i}\rho\phi\,\mathrm{d}V ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch06-dwork-template}

with $\Delta_i[\cdot]$ the difference of a face quantity across cell $i$ and $A$ the $x_1$ face area.

**The booked work.** Pick any discrete potential energy $P=\sum_iP_i$ and *define* the booked work by

$$
W_iV_i := -\dot P_i - \Delta_i[A\phi F],
$$ {#eq-ch06-dwork-booked}

with $\dot P_i$ evaluated on the discrete density tendency and $W$ in W m$^{-3}$. Two properties follow.
**Conservation:** summing @eq-ch06-dwork-booked over a column, the $\Delta_i$ terms telescope to the two walls,
where $F=0$, so $\sum_iW_iV_i + \dot P = 0$; the other energy fluxes telescope too, so $E+P$ is conserved exactly,
whatever $P$ is. **Accuracy:** subtracting @eq-ch06-dwork-booked from @eq-ch06-dwork-template gives
$W_iV_i - g_1V_i\langle F\rangle_{V_i} = \tfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(\mathcal P_i - P_i)$, so the booked work is
exactly as accurate as $P_i$ is as an approximation of the cell's potential energy.

The forms differ only in $P$. The face form takes the piecewise-constant $P=\mathrm{PE}_d$ (@sec-ch06-face); the
corrected-PE face work takes a fourth-order $P$ (@sec-ch06-dwork); the cell form starts from no $P$ and leaves a
defect that the fixer removes (@sec-ch06-cell, @sec-ch06-fixer). The implicit solver carries the same work in its
energy row (@sec-ch06-vic), and @sec-ch06-conserves collects which invariant each form keeps.
